conditioning.name: Pre-Match Prop Primer
conditioning.purpose: Create a short sharp pre-match stimulus without soreness or meaningful fatigue.

parts.name: Choose one location option
parts.detail: Complete either the gym-equipment option or the field/no-equipment option for the whole session. Do not combine the two.

parts.name: Gym option
parts.detail: 5 min easy machine build-up; then 5 x 8 sec fast air-bike or rower efforts with 60-75 sec easy recovery; finish with 3 x 3 low box jumps or explosive step jumps with full reset.

parts.name: Field option
parts.detail: 5 min easy jog and progressive movement; then 3 x 10 m relaxed-to-fast accelerations with full walk-back recovery; finish with 2 x 3 broad jumps and 2 x 10 sec fast-feet efforts.

conditioning.howToUse: Friday before each listed Saturday match. The primer replaces Friday strength.

conditioning.name: Prop Speed Microdose

parts.name: Choose one location option
parts.detail: Complete either the gym-equipment option or the field/no-equipment option for the whole session. Do not combine the two.

parts.name: Gym option
parts.detail: 10 min progressive machine build-up; then 4 x 10 sec and 4 x 15 sec fast efforts on an air bike or rower with 90-120 sec very easy recovery; stop before output drops.

parts.name: Field option
parts.detail: 10 min progressive field preparation; then 4 x 10 m and 4 x 20 m accelerations at about 90-95% with 90-120 sec walk-back/full recovery; stop before speed drops.

conditioning.howToUse: Use on a non-match Saturday when speed quality is wanted without a hard conditioning load.

conditioning.name: Prop Acceleration Microdose

parts.name: Choose one location option

parts.name: Gym option
parts.detail: 8-10 min easy machine build-up; then 6 x 10 sec powerful efforts on an air bike, rower or ski erg with 80-90 sec very easy recovery; finish with 3 x 3 explosive box jumps with full reset.

parts.name: Field option
parts.detail: 8-10 min progressive running preparation; then 6 x 10 m accelerations at 85-90% with full walk-back recovery; finish with 3 x 3 broad jumps with full reset.

conditioning.howToUse: Selected non-rugby Saturdays in the early build. Stop while output is sharp.

parts.detail: 10 min progressive machine build-up; then 2 sets of 5 x 15 sec hard sled push, air-bike or rower effort with 45 sec easy recovery; rest 3 min between sets; finish with 5 min easy on the same modality.

parts.name: Field option
parts.detail: 10 min progressive field preparation; then 2 sets of 5 reps: 10 m acceleration out, 10 m controlled shuttle back, 1 ground get-up, then walk until 45 sec has elapsed; rest 3 min between sets; finish with 5 min easy walking.

conditioning.howToUse: Use on non-match Saturdays. Keep output repeatable rather than maximal.

conditioning.name: Prop Repeat-Effort Conditioning
conditioning.purpose: Develop the ability to repeat short high-output efforts with incomplete rest.

parts.name: Choose one location option
parts.detail: Complete either the gym-equipment option or the field/no-equipment option for the whole session. Do not combine the two.

parts.name: Gym option
parts.detail: 10 min progressive warm-up on one machine; then 2 sets of 5 x 30 sec hard on bike, rower or ski erg with 45 sec very easy recovery; rest 3 min between sets; finish with 6-8 min easy.

parts.name: Field option
parts.detail: 10 min progressive field preparation; then 2 sets of 5 reps: 10 m acceleration, controlled floor get-up, 10 m shuttle back; rest until 45 sec has elapsed; rest 3 min between sets; finish with 6-8 min easy walk.

conditioning.howToUse: Selected non-match Saturdays. Use one full location option only.

conditioning.name: Fitness Performance Check
conditioning.purpose: Track speed and conditioning without combining barbell strength testing with conditioning.

parts.name: Choose one location option
parts.detail: Complete either the gym-equipment option or the field/no-equipment option for the whole session. Do not combine the two.

parts.name: Gym option
parts.detail: 10-12 min progressive machine build-up; record best of 3 x 10 sec peak-output efforts on the same machine with full recovery; then complete 6 min steady-hard and record distance/calories.

parts.name: Field option
parts.detail: 10-12 min progressive field preparation; record best of 3 x 10 m accelerations using a consistent timing setup when available; then complete 6 min of repeatable 20 m shuttles and record total distance.

conditioning.howToUse: Use the same location option in May and July. Strength markers are logged separately during normal strength blocks.

conditioning.name: Off-Season Speed Microdose
conditioning.purpose: Maintain and improve short-burst speed after rugby ends without turning the session into fatigue-based conditioning.

parts.name: Choose one location option
parts.detail: Complete either the gym-equipment option or the field/no-equipment option for the whole session. Do not combine the two.

parts.name: Gym option
parts.detail: 8-10 min progressive easy machine work; then 4 x 10 sec and 3 x 15 sec fast efforts on an air bike, rower or ski erg with 90-120 sec very easy recovery; stop if output falls.

parts.name: Field option
parts.detail: 8-10 min progressive field preparation; then 4 x 10 m and 3 x 20 m accelerations at approximately 90-95% with 90-120 sec full recovery; stop if mechanics deteriorate.

conditioning.howToUse: Most Tuesdays from May to mid-July. This session and Off-Season Lower A must be in separate day-blocks.

conditioning.name: Anaerobic Repeats
conditioning.purpose: Build high-intensity anaerobic repeatability without forcing one training location.

parts.name: Choose one location option
parts.detail: Complete either the gym-equipment option or the field/no-equipment option for the whole session. Do not combine the two.

parts.name: Gym option
parts.detail: 10 min progressive easy-to-moderate work on bike, rower or ski erg; 8 x 30 sec hard with 90 sec very easy on the same machine; 10 min easy.

parts.name: Field option
parts.detail: 10 min progressive walk/jog; 8 x 30 sec hard shuttle running over 15-20 m with 90 sec walking recovery; 10 min easy walk.

conditioning.howToUse: Selected Saturdays after rugby. Keep the first six efforts repeatable.

conditioning.name: Cruise Treadmill Aerobic Intervals
conditioning.purpose: Build aerobic fitness and running tolerance through controlled treadmill intervals without turning the session into an all-out effort.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: 0.5-1.0% incline. Walk 3 min @ 4.5 km/h, then 3 min @ 5.2 km/h.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: 4 min run @ 7.5 km/h, then 2 min walk @ 5.0 km/h. Keep the running controlled and repeatable.

conditioning.howToUse: Keep this comfortably below maximum effort. The aim is aerobic work and running consistency rather than testing fitness.

conditioning.name: Cruise Track Easy Run
conditioning.purpose: Finish the cruise week with an easy aerobic run that maintains running frequency without adding significant fatigue.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: 5 min brisk walking around the track.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: 20 min continuous easy running at conversational effort, approximately RPE 4-5. Ignore pace and keep the effort relaxed.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: 5 min easy walking around the track.

conditioning.howToUse: This should be the easiest running session of the week. Keep the pace deliberately comfortable and do not turn the final few laps into a harder effort.

conditioning.name: Cruise Treadmill Tempo Intervals
conditioning.purpose: Introduce slightly faster controlled running while maintaining good form and avoiding excessive fatigue.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: 0.5-1.0% incline. Walk 3 min @ 4.5 km/h, then jog 4 min @ 6.5-7.0 km/h.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: 3 min controlled hard run @ 8.0 km/h, then 2 min easy walk @ 5.0 km/h. Aim for approximately RPE 7.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: 3 min easy walking @ 4.0-4.5 km/h.

conditioning.howToUse: This is the quicker session of the week, but it should still feel controlled. Do not increase the speed if your running form starts to deteriorate.

conditioning.name: Post-Cruise Treadmill Conditioning
conditioning.purpose: Provide a challenging but controlled return-to-training session after the cruise, building aerobic power and sustained running capacity without requiring an all-out effort.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: 0.5-1.0% incline. Walk 3 min @ 4.5 km/h, then 4 min @ 5.2-5.5 km/h.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: 5 min run @ 7.8-8.0 km/h, then 2 min walk @ 5.0 km/h. The running should feel strong and purposeful but remain controlled throughout.

parts.name: Controlled finish
parts.detail: Run 2 min @ 8.0 km/h if you still feel smooth and controlled. Skip this section if the four main repetitions were already around RPE 8.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk 3 min @ 4.0-4.5 km/h.

conditioning.howToUse: Aim for around RPE 7-8 during the running blocks. The final repetition should be difficult but still look like normal running rather than survival. Keep the treadmill at 7.8 km/h if you feel heavy after travelling; use 8.0 km/h only if the first two repetitions feel controlled.

mobility.name: Pre-Run Dynamic Mobility
mobility.purpose: Prepare the hips, ankles and legs for running or sprinting.

parts.name: Walking knee hugs
parts.detail: 10 steps per side

parts.name: Walking quad pulls
parts.detail: 10 steps per side

parts.name: Leg swings
parts.detail: 10 forward-and-back and 10 side-to-side per leg

parts.name: Walking lunges with rotation
parts.detail: 8 reps per side

parts.name: A-march
parts.detail: 2 x 15 metres

parts.name: Pogo jumps
parts.detail: 2 x 15 light reps

mobility.howToUse: Complete immediately before running, sprinting or field training.

mobility.name: Post-Training Mobility
mobility.purpose: Help the body settle after training and reduce feelings of lower-body tightness.

parts.name: Half-kneeling hip-flexor stretch
parts.detail: 60 seconds per side

parts.name: Hamstring stretch
parts.detail: 60 seconds per side

parts.name: Figure-four glute stretch
parts.detail: 60 seconds per side

parts.name: Adductor stretch
parts.detail: 60 seconds per side

parts.name: Calf stretch
parts.detail: 45 seconds per side

parts.name: Relaxed breathing
parts.detail: 2 minutes, slow breaths through the nose

mobility.howToUse: Perform after gym, rugby or running sessions. Keep every position comfortable rather than forcing the stretch.

parts.name: Wall slides
parts.detail: 2 x 10 reps

mobility.name: Lower-Body Mobility
mobility.purpose: Prepare the hips, ankles and calves for squatting, running and rugby.

parts.name: 90/90 hip switches
parts.detail: 2 x 8 reps

parts.name: Knee-to-wall ankle rocks
parts.detail: 2 x 10 reps per side

parts.name: Deep squat hold
parts.detail: 2 x 30 seconds

parts.name: Slow calf raises
parts.detail: 2 x 10 reps

mobility.name: Pre-Match Mobility Primer
mobility.purpose: Prepare hips, ankles, thoracic spine and shoulders for a short pre-match primer without creating fatigue.

parts.name: Ankle rocks
parts.detail: 10 per side

parts.name: Leg swings
parts.detail: 10 each direction per side

parts.name: Walking lunge and rotation
parts.detail: 6 per side

parts.name: A-march
parts.detail: 2 x 10 m

mobility.howToUse: Immediately before the Friday Pre-Match Prop Primer.

recovery.name: Post-Training Recovery Routine
recovery.purpose: Begin the recovery process immediately after a demanding gym, running or rugby session.
recovery.notes: Complete 10 minutes of easy walking or cycling, drink water, eat a meal containing protein and carbohydrates, then spend the remainder relaxing.

recovery.name: Sunday Complete Rest
recovery.purpose: Provide a genuine recovery day after Saturday rugby or cardio.
recovery.notes: No formal training. Normal daily movement is fine. Prioritise sleep, food and hydration.

recovery.name: Wednesday Recovery
recovery.purpose: Recover between Tuesday and Thursday rugby training.
recovery.notes: Easy walk or very easy cycle only. Keep the effort restorative.

recovery.name: Sauna Recovery Optional
recovery.purpose: Provide optional relaxation without adding mechanical training stress.
recovery.notes: Use only when well hydrated. Sauna never replaces sleep, food or fluid.

recovery.name: Rugby Sleep Downshift
recovery.purpose: Bring physical and mental arousal down after late Tuesday/Thursday rugby training so recovery starts without adding more exercise and sleep is easier.
recovery.notes: This is the only planned activity after Tuesday/Thursday evening rugby. Once it is finished, go straight into normal bedtime preparation: low light, no training, no mobility session, no conditioning and ideally no stimulating screen use.
